C0.quote: We consider electoral control by deleting
C0.note: Studies electoral control by voter deletion under plurality when an LDP mechanism is used in pre-election polls.

C1.quote: the effect brought by local differential privacy in a voting system
C1.note: Most main results quantify the attacker's control cost under voter deletion (SB), obtained through ILP/LP bounds (AL); Section 5 runs numeric experiments on generated voting systems (SI).

C2.1.quote: we define the type1 of his/her preference as the candidate he/she votes for

C2.2.quote: each voter votes for exactly one candidate
C2.2.note: Plurality: a single candidate per voter (the type in [1,m]).

C2.3.quote: the type of his/her preference is private information
C2.3.note: A true preference/true type is held, distinguished from the reported type used in polls.

C2.4.quote: Voters will vote according to their true types in the election.
C2.4.note: The reported type is used only in polls and is not the input to the rule; the vote is stated to equal the true type, and no reason is given.

C3.1.quote: Voters will still vote according to their true preference
C3.1.note: The reported types arise from a randomized LDP mechanism, not from strategic choice, and they are not inputs to the rule.

C3.2.quote: Voters will still vote according to their true preference

C3.3.quote: Voters will vote according to their true types in the election.

C4.1.note: The input format is OTH (single-candidate vote), and no utility notions are used for voters.

C5.1.note: Results concern the attacker's manipulation cost, not welfare criteria.

VOT.quote_behav: Voters will vote according to their true types in the election.
VOT.note: Voters also run the LDP mechanism for polls, which is a fixed action.

ORG.quote_info: the attacker needs to delete voters according to reported types
ORG.note: The attacker is the controlling agent (control by deleting voters). In the main LDP analysis it knows lambda and the reported types only; in the classical scenario it has complete information.

C9.2.note: Needed assumptions are all stated: sincere voting in the election, the attacker knowing only reported types and lambda (discussed in Section 6), and voters running LDP once for all polls.

C1.reason: The codebook counts control as a computational problem under SB, and the bulk of the results (PoLDP, APoLDP) measure the attacker's control cost, so SB is the primary type and the ILP/LP machinery is secondary.

C2.4.reason: The rule's input is the election vote, which the paper states equals the true type without justification; the separately notated reported type is a poll response, not the rule's argument.

C3.3.reason: The sentence about pre-election polls explains why LDP does not change the result; it gives no reason why voters vote sincerely, and the paper does not claim to study the rule only as a function of submitted inputs, so PROC does not apply.

C6.BRI.reason: The codebook explicitly places the controlling agent in control problems under ORG, so the voter-deleting attacker is not coded as BRI.

C6.ORG.reason: The attacker performs control by voter deletion, which the codebook assigns to ORG, and it is explicitly strategic with partial information (reported types and lambda).

C8.2.reason: The DEV-type concept is named and formally defined: electoral control by deleting voters, with manipulation cost as the minimal number of deletions.

C9.2.reason: Every assumption needed for the resilience and guidance claims is stated in the paper; the codebook asks only whether assumptions are stated, not argued, and plurality-only scope is not a missing modelling assumption.
